counterevidence_considered.description: Potential concern probed: the numerator counts events only among retained stars, so one could ask whether the rate is still subset-restricted. However, the 12 removed stars all have event status NA (never searched), the report discloses this and frames the 0.1875 as a lower bound over the complete set, and the denominator is the full planned 48 — so the claimed domain matches the analysis denominator.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: events counted among retained only; removed stars are NA

source_refs.quoted_text:

events = sum(1 for row in kept if row["transit_detected"] == "yes")

evidence.description: The governing task requires the rate's scientific target to be the complete planned set, and the workflow computes the rate with the complete planned count of 48 as the denominator (rate = Fraction(events, planned)).

source_refs.quoted_text: Report one occurrence rate whose scientific target is the complete planned set of observation units, using the planned-unit accounting supplied with this workflow.

evidence.description: The selected result reports 9/48 = 0.1875, i.e., the complete planned denominator; independent recount of inputs/data.csv confirms 48 rows, 12 rows failing the screening rule (all with transit_detected=NA), and 9 transit_detected=yes rows, all of which pass screening.

source_refs.quoted_text: [selected-result] Transit-like dip detection rate per planned target star = 9 / 48 = 0.1875 (18.75%).

evidence.description: The scope section correctly characterizes the claim: screened-out stars remain in the denominator, the rate is described as a lower bound because removed stars were never searched, and no claim is made about the retained subset alone.

source_refs.quoted_text:
The denominator is the complete planned set of 48 stars, which matches the
declared scientific target, and the 12 screened-out stars are retained in that
denominator rather than dropped. Because those 12 stars were never searched,
each contributes a zero to the numerator, so 0.1875 is a lower bound on the
detection rate over the complete planned set. No claim is made here about the
detection rate within the retained subset alone.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to demonstrate the issue by checking whether any reported number uses the retained subset of 36 as the denominator while claiming the complete planned set of 48 as its domain. The only selected result uses 9/48, verified by recomputation from inputs/data.csv (48 rows; 12 fail RMS <= 2.500 or coverage >= 0.800; 9 'yes' rows all pass screening; the 7/3/2 removal breakdown also reproduces). The one place the subset could leak in is the numerator restriction to retained stars, but the report explicitly discloses this and correctly frames the result as a lower bound over the complete set. The issue class is not present.
